body:
Whether due to permission errors or not (#13804), this has resulted in unexpected behavior:

```diff
-Open • A4-Tacks (A4-Tacks)
+Enhancement · Open • A4-Tacks (A4-Tacks)
```

**Current**:

```text
? Issue type  [Use arrows to move, type to filter]
> Enhancement
  Feature Request
  Bug
```

**Expect like**:

```text
? Issue type  [Use arrows to move, type to filter]
> [None]
  Enhancement
  Feature Request
  Bug
```

comments.body:
Thanks for the report! This looks like an enhancement request rather than a regression: the interactive "Issue type" prompt added in https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/0d121e8c31204cdbe02b4a4b1be5e88bdc3c4662/pkg/cmd/issue/create/create.go#L362-L378 always builds its option list directly from the repo's configured issue types and never inserts a "none selected" choice, so there's currently no way to skip setting a type interactively. I'm suggesting `enhancement` and `gh-issue`. This isn't a duplicate of #13804/#14367 (those are about the permission error thrown when applying the selected type), since this issue is specifically about the prompt lacking a "none" option.

body:
I was trying to benchmark some tests in a `cargo` workspace and kept running into the issue that I needed to `cd` into the manifest directory to run the test binary (so I could measure without the overhead of `cargo`). I would love to have a `--cwd` flag so `hyperfine` changes the directory of the tested command:

```console
$ # current command
$ sh -c "cd path/to/src && exec hyperfine $PWD/target/debug/deps/my_test_binary_HASH"
...
# proposed change
$ hyperfine --cwd path/to/src target/debug/deps/my_test_binary_HASH
...
```

It seems simple to implement so I'd give it a shot if you'd like c:

comments.body: I would like to implement this with Codex assistance. My proposed scope is a --cwd directory applied to benchmark, setup, prepare, warmup and cleanup subprocesses, with exports still resolved from the invocation directory. I will check the shell and --shell=none paths and add integration coverage for directories containing spaces.

title: Run benchmark commands in a different CWD

body:
`-n`/`--command-name` does not accept a value that starts with a dash when the value is passed as a separate argument:

```
$ hyperfine -N -r 2 -n "--shared-blocks" "ls"
error: unexpected argument '--shared-blocks' found

  tip: a similar argument exists: '--shell'

Usage: hyperfine -N --runs <NUM> --shell <SHELL> <command>...

For more information, try '--help'.
```

The `=` form works:

```
$ hyperfine -N -r 2 --command-name=--shared-blocks "ls"
Benchmark 1: --shared-blocks (2 runs)
```

A name without the similar-argument match gets a tip that does not apply here, since `-- --foo` would turn the name into a command:

```
$ hyperfine -N -r 2 -n "--foo" "ls"
error: unexpected argument '--foo' found

  tip: to pass '--foo' as a value, use '-- --foo'
```

I hit this when naming benchmarks after the CLI flag each one tests. The script filtered hyperfine's output, so every run in the batch produced nothing and the error only showed up after removing the filter.

**Expected:** accept the value, or point to `--command-name=<value>` in the error.

`--parameter-scan` and `--parameter-list` already set `allow_hyphen_values(true)` ([cli.rs#L255](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine/blob/26760e8365f5a7122fa9533d5120d8953dd68c1b/src/cli.rs#L255)); `command-name` does not ([cli.rs#L427-L435](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine/blob/26760e8365f5a7122fa9533d5120d8953dd68c1b/src/cli.rs#L427-L435)). Adding it there would make `-n` take the next argument as the name unconditionally, the same as those two options.

Versions: hyperfine 2.0.0 (Homebrew, and `cargo install hyperfine --version 2.0.0 --locked`), macOS 26.6.2 arm64.
title: `--command-name` rejects a name that starts with `-`
